tiers.1: scholarly work by economists, in any venue: journal articles, working papers, books, chapters, commission reports, and their essays or articles in magazines. "Economist" means an economics appointment, degree, address or affiliation shown in or near the text, or an established record as an economist. Anything in a core economics venue (top five, JEP, JEL, AER P&P, NBER working papers and the NBER Economics of AI volume) is tier 1 regardless of author.
tiers.2: texts by non-economists, whatever the venue, and short-form commentary even by economists (blog comments, forum replies, magazine or online debates, unless a turn is itself a substantive scholarly argument).
tiers.decision: Maintainer decision of 2026-10-11 (README D2), shared with the economics-growth pack. It replaces the rule of 2026-10-09, under which magazines were tier 2 whatever the author. Each source and lead carries a one-line tierBasis.

relations.articulates: the passage meets the proposition's criterion
relations.contests: the passage disputes the proposition or a premise it depends on; engagement required
relations.bears-on: the passage bears on the proposition without meeting the criterion; missing names the gap

propositions.statement: Machine intelligence could improve itself, or the design of its successors, in a way that accelerates its own capability growth.
propositions.criterion: A text that states or models AI systems improving AI (their own capabilities, their successors' design, or AI research itself) so that capability growth accelerates. Accelerating output growth from automated idea production without AI improving AI is the economics-growth pack's G02 and only bears on E01.

propositions.statement: Machine intelligence could come to exceed human cognitive ability in essentially all domains.
propositions.criterion: A text that states or models the possibility of machine intelligence that surpasses humans across essentially all cognitive tasks (superintelligence, AGI beyond human level). Machines doing all economically valuable work more cheaply is M05 in the main pack and bears on E02 only if cognitive superiority is stated.

propositions.statement: Advanced AI poses a risk of human extinction or permanent loss of control that belongs in economic analysis.
propositions.criterion: A text that treats existential or catastrophic risk from AI (extinction, loss of control, misaligned goals) as a quantity or consideration in economic analysis, welfare trade-offs or policy.

propositions.statement: Developers of advanced AI face incentives (racing, competition, governance structures) that matter for its safety.
propositions.criterion: A text that analyses how incentives, competition or governance of AI developers affect the safety or control of advanced AI.

propositions.statement: Economics has engaged with, or neglected, superintelligence, AGI and the singularity.
propositions.criterion: A passage articulates E05 only if it explicitly says something about the state of economics on the topic: that it is new, neglected, speculative, now on the agenda of economics, or beyond economists' existing tools. Economists' engagement itself is recorded under E01–E04 and in the timeline (the dated record), not here. Machine intelligence that does human jobs is not counted as AGI for E05, as for E02. Maintainer decision of 2026-10-15 (option A of the decision note in audit.md).
propositions.criterionBefore: Not a criterion for a single passage. Assessed from the dated record and from texts' explicit statements that the topic is new, neglected, speculative or now on the agenda of economics. (Until 2026-10-15.)
